big_move_followthrough.verdict: 2026-11-20: 1,094 big days (|move|>=2.5 sd or 8%) in the 10 stocks since 2019 (research/big_moves.csv), split market / sector / company-only. panic_day_rebound.verdict: 2026-11-20 PROMISING (not proven): buy at the close when the market (SPY) falls 2%+, the stock falls 3%+ and is 15%+ below its 20-day high (CCJ Nov 5 2026 type). 61 distinct days since 2019: hold 4 days +3.6% avg / +3.3% median, up 62%; hold 6 days +5.3% / +6.2%, up 70% (p=0.001 by day), positive every year. Risk: when the panic is the start of a crash (Feb-Mar 2020, May 2022) it loses 15-21% and stops don't help (gaps). Buying next morning instead of the close keeps much less (+0.9% over 2 days). ~23 variants tried, so treat as a candidate for paper testing. | 2026-11-20 filters tried (first vs repeat panic, market vs 200-day avg, market drawdown, size of market/stock drop; 10 more trials): none removes the crash days cleanly, splits are 4-15 days and flip between halves. Kept the simple rule; protection = size (15% each, 45% total, 3 names). Now trading on paper as strategy #2. | 2026-11-20 round 3 (25 more trials): which 3 to pick barely matters (deepest-under-high +6.0% vs biggest-drop +5.3%, noise); VIX 40+ days best (+9.3%, 85% up, n=13); SECTOR-only panics have no edge (+0.6%), it needs the whole market; fixed 6-day hold best avg, but sell at +10% close or day 6 = +5.0% avg, 72% up, worst -17.5% (vs -21.4%) and frees cash sooner -> adopted. Non-panic swings: best is -10% in 3 days in a calm market, +2.1% over 6d vs +1.0% for any day, steady in both halves (practice candidate only). | 2026-11-23 exits (3 trials, 153 trades on 61 days): sell at +10% on a CLOSE or day 6 = +5.8% avg (71% up) beats a resting +10% limit (+4.4%, 75% up), a +8% limit (+3.7%) and a give-back guard (+5.5%); both halves agree. Winners often run past +10%, so selling intraday cuts them. No change: keep the close rule, no stop (crash-day gaps go straight through stops). | 2026-11-23 sizing (5 trials, $1,000 compounded 2019-2026 incl. 2020 crash): 15%/45% -> $2,248 (10.8%/yr, worst drop -16.5%); 25%/75% -> $3,666 (17.9%, -26.8%); 33%/100% -> $5,023 (22.7%, -34.5%); 50%/100% -> $5,832 (25.0%, -45.2%); 100% one name -> $10,767 (35.1%, -45.5%, only 44 trades: rides on single picks). Every year positive at every size. Owner chose to compound harder: ADOPTED 33% each / 100% total on paper. Panic days are rare (75 of 1,985 sessions), so cash sits idle most days; 3-down-days as an idle-cash setup: +1.66% over 5d vs +0.84% any day, 55% up, too weak alone. | 2026-11-23 adaptive size (13 trials: VIX bands, SPY vs 200d, depth, stock drop; 2 size tables): VIX<25 +7.3% (77% up), VIX 25-40 +2-3% (weakest), VIX 40+ +11.7% (83%); stock -8%+ +7.9% vs -3-5% +3.7%. Steps 10/15/25/40/50% by VIX zone + stock drop: $1,000 -> $5,863 (25.1%/yr, worst drop -23.2%) vs flat 33% $5,018 (-34.5%). Gain is mostly in the older half (newer 1.62x vs 1.64x), so the main win is the smaller drawdown. Same data used to pick the bands: in-sample. ADOPTED with the PM allowed one step up/down after the team talks; each PM size call is scored vs the rule (pm_size_score). | 2026-11-23 intraday caps on top of the close rule (+15/+20/+25% resting sells): +5.2/+5.6/+5.8% vs +5.8% without; no gain, kept as is. Trades that touched +10% intraday but closed below (62 of 153): finished +10.7% avg, 92% up, 66% ended at +10% or more -> holding through that dip is right. | 2026-11-23 profit-lock stops (after a close at +5/+6/+8%, stop at 0/+2/+3%, gap fills at the open): avg +4.8 to +5.3% vs +5.8% without, worst trade unchanged (-27.9%: crash trades never go up first). Not adopted. | 2026-11-23 WIDER UNIVERSE (same rule, $20M+/day and $3+ filter, 0.1% cost, best 3 by depth): nuclear 10: 83 trades +3.45% avg 64% up (older -0.1, newer +6.9); ~74 related stocks: 183 trades +3.95% 66% up (older +2.5, newer +5.4), every year positive; combined 191 trades +3.96%. By group: new nuclear +8.3% (39), AI/data-center +4.3% (131), grid equipment +4.1% (90), mining +3.3% (89), nuclear utilities +2.7% (44), defense +1.6% (36), gas +1.0% (78, worst -62%), builders +0.5% (56). Compounding (adaptive size, cash idle): nuclear only $1,955 (8.9%/yr, -18.7%) vs nuclear first + related fill $2,782 (13.8%/yr, -26.3%). ADOPTED on paper: nuclear picks first, empty slots from the related list. Note: this test's liquidity filter is stricter than the first panic test, so absolute numbers are lower than the earlier 25%/yr; compare within the test.

ccj_daily_reversal.verdict: 2026-11-20: CCJ day-to-day moves are close to random (autocorrelation -0.02). After up/down days of 3-5%, 5-8%, 8%+ and gap-and-reverse days, the next 1-3 days show no reliable bounce-back (p 0.19-0.95). The 'jumps up then back down' pattern is visible but not predictable from the day's move alone; across all 10 stocks, company-only up spikes do fade (see big_move_followthrough).

panic_rebound_calls_estimate.verdict: 2026-11-20 ESTIMATE (Black-Scholes, implied vol = 1.3x recent vol on entry, 1.05x on exit, ~5% spread each way; no real historical option prices): 2-week calls on the panic-day picks turn the stock's +5.2% into about +5% (at the money) or 0% (5% out of the money) on average, median -9% to -16%, winning on <50% of days, losing 80%+ on 11-15%. Fear makes options expensive exactly on panic days. Shares beat calls for this setup. Re-test with the options recorder's real chains once enough panic days are recorded. Today's real CCJ chain: IV ~60%, $65 Dec-4 call 0.65/0.97 (40% spread).

news_pop_fade.verdict: 2026-11-23 (15 nuclear stocks, 1999-2026, 400 stock-specific jumps of +8%+ on 2x volume with SPY under +2%, one per 10 days): all pops: median 5d -0.8%, 20d -3.0%, 43% up after 20 days, but averages near normal (fat right tail) and the halves disagree (pre-2019 faded, 2019+ didn't). Jumps of +15%+ (n=129): 5d median -3.5% older / -1.4% newer, 20d median -8.6% / -5.1%, both halves agree. 8-15% jumps: halves disagree. 2026: 14 of 20 pops lower 20 days later. Related universe (63 stocks, 1,222 events) shows no fade. Adopted: no conviction buys within 5 sessions of a +15% one-day jump (pop_guard). Not adopted: shorting/puts after pops (mean 20d return +0.3%, the right tail makes it a losing bet on average).

open_order_timing.verdict: 2026-11-23 (13 nuclear stocks, hourly bars Dec 2023-Nov 2026, 9,158 stock-days): the first hour is weak on average (-0.2 to -0.3%) on every gap size except gap-downs of 2%+ (+0.3%, halves disagree). Its low sits 2-3% under the open. Limit buys 1-3% under the open: ~80% of first-hour fills trade at the limit again after 10:30 anyway, and the ~20% that only fill in the first hour are the best trades (+4.5% to +5.2% by the close). So waiting until 10:30 gets no better price and drops the best fills. Kept: orders go in at 9:31 after the open prints (setups the open already broke are dropped first). Not adopted: orders before the bell (they fill at the open even when the stock gaps through support).

power_deal_events.verdict: 2026-11-23 (7 big-tech nuclear power deals, Mar 2024-Oct 2026: AWS-Talen x2, Microsoft/Meta/Amazon/Google-Constellation, Meta-Vistra): the stock that signed rose +8.8% on the day (median +10.5%), rivals CEG/VST/TLN +5.0%, SPY +0.1%. The move happens on the day; too few deals for a rule. Adopted as alerts + context (deals.py), with the no-chase guard covering +15% days.

group_exposure_caps.verdict: 2026-11-23 (panic rule as live: nuclear first + related fill, VIX/drop sizing, +10% close exit or 6 sessions, Jan 2019-Nov 2026, 192 trades): baseline $1,000 -> $5,942, 25.3%/yr, worst drop -34.7% (Aug 2019-Mar 12 2020; the other 20%+ drop was 2022 Q2). Total caps 75/60/50%: 20.8/17.4/14.6%/yr with worst drops -30.6/-26.4/-23.4%: return per unit of drop gets worse (0.73 -> 0.68/0.66/0.62). Max 1 per group: 19.3%/yr, -36.2%; max 2 per group: 23.5%/yr, -34.9%. Correlation-triggered caps (picks' 60-day correlation 0.6-0.7+ -> 40-60%): 19.6-23.5%/yr, worst drop unchanged at -34.7%. The big drops are market-wide crashes where everything falls together, not picks that resemble each other, so diversifying picks doesn't help. Not adopted; VIX-based sizing stays the protection.
